Choose one ability score. It increases by 4 for 8 hours, with no maximum.
Choose one ability score. It increases by 6 for 8 hours, with no maximum.
You gain one full level in one class for 24 hours, including Hit Points, Spell Slots, prepared spells, and class features. This can raise your total level above 20.
You gain two full levels in one or more classes and increase one chosen ability score by 2 for 24 hours. These increases have no maximum and can raise your total level above 20.

table.name: Flawed Ioun Stone Effects
rows: {@b Bad Luck.} Subtract 1 from your attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, and each damage die, to a minimum of 1 damage per die. Modify percentile rolls by 10 against your interests. A super-charged flaw applies -2 and 20 percentage points.

{@b Interference.} Each spell you cast has a 20 percent chance to fail. Rogue skill checks take a -4 penalty, weapon attacks take a -2 penalty, and you take a -2 penalty to AC because of spasms and distracting noise only you hear.
{@b Paralysis.} Whenever you activate the stone's normal property, roll {@dice 1d100}. On 20 or lower, you have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.
{@b Blindness.} In a stressful moment, make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw with a -2 penalty. On a failure, Positive or Negative Energy blinds you for 1 minute.

{@b Transference.} Once every 7 days, if another creature is within 20 feet, roll {@dice 1d100}. On 20 or lower, the stone immediately bonds to and orbits a random creature in range, carrying this flaw and one additional flaw with it.

{@b Ethereal Slippage.} In a stressful moment, roll {@dice 1d100}. On 20 or lower, you slip into the Border Ethereal for 3 rounds and can take no actions. Ethereal creatures can perceive and attack you.
{@b Level Nullification.} Your effective level decreases by 1, to a minimum of 1, and you can't gain Experience Points while the stone remains bonded.
{@b Obstruction.} The stone continually darts through your field of view. The DM can impose Disadvantage on sight-based checks or Concentration checks when its distraction matters.

{@b Ability Reduction.} At each dawn, roll {@dice 1d6}. The corresponding ability score decreases by {@dice 2d4} for 24 hours, to a minimum of 1: 1 Strength, 2 Intelligence, 3 Wisdom, 4 Constitution, 5 Dexterity, 6 Charisma. It can't reduce an ability the stone normally increases.
{@b Uncontrolled Growth.} Your hair grows {@dice 1d12} inches and your fingernails grow 2 inches each day.
{@b Sneezing.} When you activate the stone, succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or sneeze uncontrollably, delaying its property by 3 rounds.
{@b Clumsiness.} When your attack roll is a natural 1 or 2, you drop one held item after the attack resolves.
{@b Stress Muteness.} In a stressful moment, make a DC 18 Charisma saving throw with a -2 penalty. On a failure, you can't speak for 1 minute.
{@b Stolen Healing.} Subtract 1 from each die rolled by a spell to restore your Hit Points, to a minimum of 1 per die. A super-charged flaw subtracts 2 per die.

{@b Cowardice.} When you are targeted by a spell of level 3 or higher, the stone burrows into a pouch, pack, or other container you carry. Its normal benefit ends until it returns to orbit after the spell resolves.
{@b Reversed Energy.} At each dawn, reduce your Hit Point maximum by {@dice 2d4 + 2}. Reroll the reduction each day; it isn't cumulative and ends when the bond ends.
{@b Fear of Darkness.} While in Dim Light or Darkness, you have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition unless a Continual Flame or equally bright magical light is within sight.
{@b Multitude of Maladies.} Your skin changes bright colors, you smell of cooking sauerkraut, and nonmagical leather, paper, wood, and other organic objects you wear slowly decay.
{@b Violent Orbit.} When another creature first moves within 10 feet of you, roll {@dice 1d20}. On 18-20, the stone strikes it for {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage.
{@b Nullifying Flaw.} Every other Ioun Stone orbiting you becomes dormant until this flawed stone's bond ends.
{@b Crystalline Warts.} Large crystal growths form across your body whenever the stone is activated. They fade slowly but return larger after each activation.
{@b Energy Attraction.} When another Ioun Stone comes within 20 feet, roll {@dice 1d100}. On 5 or lower, it abandons its current orbit and immediately bonds to you.
{@b Daily Size Shift.} At each dawn, your height and dimensions increase or decrease by 25 percent, chosen randomly, until the next dawn. Nonmagical armor doesn't resize.
{@b Garble-Tongue.} Under stress, you can speak only unintelligible sounds. You can't provide Verbal spell components until the stressful situation ends.
{@b Weapon Discord.} An intelligent magic weapon you possess becomes hostile to you. Attacks with it take a -2 penalty to attack and damage rolls.
{@b Missile Magnet.} Whenever a physical ranged attack is made during combat and you are an eligible target, roll {@dice 1d100}. On 20 or lower, the attack targets you instead.

{@b Shard Scream.} Whenever you activate the stone, roll {@dice 1d100}. On 5 or lower, it screams and summons a huge hostile {@creature Shard|MECIounStones} that attempts to kill you and recover the stone.

{@b Living Crystal.} Each activation transforms {@dice 1d4} percent of your body into living crystal, starting at the extremities. Remove Curse doesn't reverse it; Stone to Flesh does. At 100 percent, you are transported to the Quasi-Elemental Plane of Mineral and lost.
{@b Field of Loathing.} Another creature attempting to move within 10 feet of you must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw or be unable to approach you for 1 minute.
{@b Reversed Orbit.} In a stressful moment, the stone becomes fixed in space for 1 minute, and you helplessly orbit it while remaining within 3 feet.

table.name: Mineral Plane Encounters
rows: The walls and floor open as Trolls attack. Their rocky bodies have AC 17 and can't be ignited; replace their Fire weakness with a vulnerability to Thunder damage.
A pool of microcrystals erupts. Each Sandling's abrasive crystals increase its attack damage by one die and its AC by 2. Alternatively, one triple-sized Sandling attacks.
The party has approached a guard post high on a gorge wall. Unless they have permission to travel here, the Giants attack, perhaps with crystalline cave-bear allies.
The tunnel walls animate. These specimens have 10 Hit Point Dice, and their Bite deals {@damage 3d6 + 4} Piercing damage.
Far from the Plane of Fire, these Salamanders aid the party if doing so serves their interests.
Roaming Xorn demand refined metals, especially armor, shields, and weapons.
A mass of Margoyles attacks through the surrounding stone from every direction. A creature they carry away can be abandoned inside solid rock.
Crystal formations animate and swarm intruders, retreating only after half their number is destroyed.
A twelve-headed, 16-Hit-Die Stone Hydra rises from the ground. Its AC can be as high as 24, its Bite deals {@damage 1d10 + 4}, and every third round it exhales a 20-foot-radius petrifying gas cloud.

These nearly transparent scorpions impose a -2 penalty on attacks against them among crystals. A stinger breaks off on a hit, imposing -4 AC until removed. Alternatively, use half as many with doubled Hit Point Dice.
Tapping leads to a gemstone quarry operated by roaming Pech. Respectful travelers may receive directions or aid.
Drow, Githyanki, Humans, or another prepared expedition seeks Ioun Stones. Their equipment becomes treasure if defeated, so the DM should design this encounter deliberately.
A quarry miles across blocks the route. Thousands of slaves labor under Dao overseers building a passage to another reality. Passage requires negotiation or payment.
The Galeb Duhr commune with a node of Earth power and react violently to disturbances that threaten its aura.
Clicking echoes from side tunnels before Hook Horrors converge. One tunnel provides a shortcut around a dangerous region if found.
A destructive cluster attacks every creature approaching its territory, fighting for the pleasure of devastation.
Crystal Umber Hulks burst from the tunnel. Double a standard Umber Hulk's Hit Points, set AC to 20, and double its Claw and Mandible damage dice.
The Elementals carry a message to or from Crystalle. Proper respect may earn the party aid or safe passage.
A 16-Hit-Die Para-Elemental rises from a sulfurous magma pool and demands valuable magic or treasure as payment for passage.
With tremendous grinding, the passage collapses as a new horizontal tunnel or vertical shaft opens. Its ancient-looking crystal formations were created only moments ago.

entries.name: Publication Note
entries: This is a 2024 5e conversion of Matthew Hargenrader's 104-page AD&D supplement. The original publication date is unknown; 2026-08-01 records this digital conversion. The conversion preserves relative power and peculiarities first, using modern terminology and action structure without reducing effects merely because they exceed ordinary 5e item benchmarks.

entries.name: Credits
entries: Written and compiled by Matthew Hargenrader. Interior illustrations in the source are credited to Frank Gunter, Zachery Hargenrader, Hunter Reid, Jessica Brinkley, Adam Szafranski, Jennifer Eck, Matthew Hargenrader, and Tom Baxa. Artwork isn't reproduced in this JSON; source captions and credits remain acknowledged.

entries.name: Table of Contents
entries: Pages 1-4 contain the cover, contents, and introductory illustrations. Pages 5-7 present Moorchlyne's introduction. Pages 9-13 explain Ioun Stone rules. Pages 15-77 contain six catalogs of one hundred stones each, separated by illustrated interludes. Pages 79-81 cover flawed stones. Pages 83-98 cover encounters and creatures. Pages 99-101 describe the Arackle. Pages 102-104 contain the afterword and final Vancian origin note.

entries.name: Page 2: The Zaeranni
entries: The source depicts the mysterious Zaeranni dwelling within crystal beyond the shimmering Portal of Worlds.

entries.name: Page 4: Crystalle's Regal Form
entries: Crystalle often assumes a regal crystalline figure when negotiating with outsiders. Whatever shape he chooses, his cloud of Ioun Stones remains.

entries.name: The Caverns of Drak-Kientor
entries: Quann'Ra-Tioll Moorchlyne recalls encountering Ioun Stones at sixteen, after leaving his mentor Talmun Forion and abandoning a slow caravan for adventure. In Drak he joined five other inexperienced explorers bound for a repeatedly changing Zaeranni complex near the Fash Domain. Four survived six days below. Among abundant treasure, Moorchlyne received a Pale Green Prism and Vibrant Purple Prism. Their warmth, pulse, orbit, and apparently living curiosity fixed the direction of his life.

entries.name: Siljameer Varooste
entries: Moorchlyne sought the reclusive mage Siljameer Varooste near the Acitian Glacier fields. At the jeweled manse, a Lavender Spindle examined the visitor and accepted him. During years of apprenticeship and later equal partnership, the pair compiled Ioun lore, visited the Quasi-Elemental Plane of Mineral at least a dozen times, and created the Arackle and many lesser Ioun devices.

entries.name: Crystalle and the Mineral Plane
entries: From lead towers along the Positive Energy boundary, Siljameer and Moorchlyne studied geode formation with {@creature Crystalle|MECIounStones}. After aiding the elemental prince, they received a geode and were permitted to choose from his immense cloud. Moorchlyne chose a Lavender Rod. Their work also exposed a connection between Ioun Stones and the ancient Zaeranni, who could apparently bond with a stone at a touch and used crystal energy throughout their portal network.

entries.name: The Final Catalog
entries: After Siljameer's death, Moorchlyne continued with assistants. He traveled widely, separating authentic stones from levitating fakes and reluctant owners' rumors. At the time of writing he claimed more than 180 bonded stones, carrying only a few dozen while the rest remained secured. This catalog is the result of those decades.

entries.name: Page 7: Ioun Greed
entries: Bazrith ignores rings, weapons, and potions while clutching one warm, bright stone and staring at the stones of his companions with growing greed.

entries.name: Page 8: Hugo Mikal III
entries: A woodcut of the 121st High Clerist of Rhamannin shows Ioun Stones surrounding the miracle-working healer's head.

data.name: General Rules and Details of Ioun Stones

entries.name: Ioun Bonds
entries: Every converted stone includes the shared {#itemEntry Moorchlyne Ioun Stone|MECIounStones} rules. A bond normally takes 7 days, is separate from ordinary attunement, and allows uncapped clouds as the source assumes. The optional {@variantrule Bounded Ioun Stones|MECIounStones} rule restores the standard 2024 three-item model.

entries.name: Magic and Ioun Stones
entries: Ioun Stones are natural, not fabricated, but channel the same Positive Energy that powers magic. Effects are suppressed by sufficiently strong antimagic and can be challenged by Magic Resistance. Dispel Magic treats a stone as a level 8 magical effect; on a successful check the stone falls dormant and requires a new bond. Antimagic suppresses a stone while it remains in the area. A Globe of Invulnerability blocks effects crossing its boundary without harming a stone. Artifact-destroying magic can permanently destroy a stone at the DM's discretion.

entries.name: Stone Types
entries: Source codes describe behavior: Instant (I) uses reactions or immediate triggers; Boosting (B) stores spells or Hit Points; Permanent (P) functions while orbiting; Voluntary (V) is deliberately activated; Limited (L) recharges on its stated cadence; Single-Use (S) crumbles after activation; Charge-Holding (C) tracks expendable charges; Temporary (T) absorbs damage or burns out. These source codes are retained in every item entry.

entries.name: Collections
entries: Duplicate color-and-shape effects don't stack unless explicitly stated. Ioun Stones resize proportionally to their bonded creature and can benefit any living, semi-intelligent being, including Familiars. Undead normally can't bond with free-floating stones, though Liches can. The benefits and dangers of large collections are detailed in {@variantrule Ioun Stone Collections|MECIounStones}.

entries.name: Geodes and Ioun Sand
entries: Ioun Stones grow inside {@item Ioun Geode|MECIounStones|Ioun Geodes} along the Positive Energy and Mineral boundary. Most geodes rupture during formation; survivors are usually recovered by elemental inhabitants. Exposure to neighboring quasi-planes can shape unusual powers. Opening a geode is lethally energetic. Its stones lie in valuable {@item Ioun Sand|MECIounStones}, which can be shaped into matrices that amplify stones.

entries.name: Using the Tables
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stone Table Selector|MECIounStones}, then roll on the selected d100 table. Every result links to its full converted item. The six tables contain exactly 600 numbered results.

entries.name: Pages 13-14
entries: The source closes the rules chapter with a creature fascinated by a hovering stone and an adventurer watching a healing stone knit wounds closed.

data.name: Table 1: Ioun Stones #001-#100
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stones #001-#100|MECIounStones}. Pages 16-23 contain the authoritative item descriptions linked by the table.

entries.name: Page 24 Interlude
entries: A scholar carefully measures a newly acquired stone through the week in which its power gradually becomes known.

data.name: Table 2: Ioun Stones #101-#200
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stones #101-#200|MECIounStones}. Pages 26-33 contain the linked descriptions.

entries.name: Page 34 Interlude
entries: A confident mage trusts the stones circling his head to overcome whatever lurks in darkness.

data.name: Table 3: Ioun Stones #201-#300
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stones #201-#300|MECIounStones}. Pages 36-44 contain the linked descriptions and the account of a Drow lord valuing two stones above the lives spent obtaining them.

data.name: Table 4: Ioun Stones #301-#400
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stones #301-#400|MECIounStones}. Pages 46-55 contain the linked descriptions.

entries.name: Page 56 Interlude
entries: A fused cluster shines red, blue, and violet with several powers held in one crystalline body.

data.name: Table 5: Ioun Stones #401-#500
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stones #401-#500|MECIounStones}. Pages 58-67 contain the linked descriptions.

entries.name: Page 68 Interlude
entries: Explorers recover more than a dozen stones hidden in an ancient dragon skull, each calling to the touch like liquid song.

data.name: Table 6: Ioun Stones #501-#600
entries: Roll on {@table Ioun Stones #501-#600|MECIounStones}. Pages 70-77 contain the linked descriptions.

entries.name: Micro Ioun Stones
entries: Stones #513-#528 and several later entries are quarter-inch micro stones whose effects are temporary or reduced. Mages value them as components in Ioun-sand matrices.

entries.name: Drusy Ioun Stones
entries: Stones #529-#544 are smooth, geode-like spell reservoirs associated with Ardrus Be-Ta'Ryu. Their dull outer crust crumbles during bonding to reveal a colored shell and internal crystal cluster. Each stores one spell of a fixed class and level.

entries.name: Pages 77-78
entries: An opened geode spills glittering sand and eight stones after a lethal expedition. On the next page, the halfling mage Fraggle Edgewise rests while playful stones circle his hat.

data.name: Flawed Ioun Stones
entries: Flawed stones are not cursed counterfeits but damaged Positive Energy conduits. Their detection, bonding, and removal rules appear in {@variantrule Flawed Ioun Stones|MECIounStones}.

Roll on {@table Flawed Ioun Stone Effects|MECIounStones}. Pages 79-81 present all thirty effects, from bad luck and spell interference to involuntary transfer, living crystallization, and reversed orbit. Additional suggested flaws include compulsive hoarding, contrariness, reduced damage dealt, reduced healing received, and increased damage taken.

entries.name: Page 82: Quaartzz
entries: A face emerges from rare metals and crystal, demanding to know who dares seek Crystalle and whether the visitors possess refined purpose.

entries.name: The Mineral Plane
entries: Prime Material creatures have elemental counterparts throughout Earth and its adjoining planes. Vast air-filled rifts serve as roads, camps, quarries, and ambush sites. Outside such pockets, visitors see nothing through solid elemental matter and move by thought rather than ordinary locomotion. The Endless Crystal Grotto may conduct Positive Energy from crystal to crystal all the way to Prime worlds.

entries.name: Mineral Plane Encounters
entries: Roll on {@table Mineral Plane Encounters|MECIounStones}. The table preserves all twenty encounters from pages 83-84.

entries.name: Crystalle
entries: {@creature Crystalle|MECIounStones} is the self-proclaimed prince of the Quasi-Elemental Plane of Mineral, a shapechanging crystalline sovereign whose intelligence and immense Ioun collection keep rivals at bay. He protects the plane's wealth, cultivates ancient geodes, bargains when it benefits him, and hopes his stones will raise him to demigodhood.

entries.name: Quaartzz
entries: {@creature Quaartzz|MECIounStones}, Crystalle's chamberlain and guardian, is an eight-foot crystal dwarf wielding a returning spear. He decides who receives an audience and commands Crystal Stone Giant wardens.

entries.name: Shard
entries: {@creature Shard|MECIounStones|Shards} are mobile, sentient crystal blades commonly found near geodes. Their swarms guard treasure, absorb Positive Energy, and may be sent to recover stolen stones.

entries.name: Glomus
entries: A {@creature Glomus|MECIounStones} is a pseudo-magnetically bound mass of crystals that glides through mineral matter, incorporates desirable crystals, explosively collapses when defeated, and reforms unless every component is shattered.

entries.name: Trilling Crysmal
entries: The {@creature Trilling Crysmal|MECIounStones} lures prey with flickering crystal light and musical trilling, then attacks with six legs and agonizing explosive darts.

entries.name: Spined Shard
entries: The {@creature Spined Shard|MECIounStones} is a cunning Positive Energy predator. It hunts ordinary Shards, lashes prey with four tentacles, injects destructive energy, and fires beams that arc between victims.

entries.name: Stilted Crysmal
entries: The {@creature Stilted Crysmal|MECIounStones} is an intelligent crystal hunter that feeds on quartz, beryl, corundum, and especially diamonds, attacking with long legs and shard volleys.

entries.name: Chamrol
entries: A {@creature Chamrol|MECIounStones} is a stationary, lead-skinned mineral organism rooted along the Positive Energy boundary. Its immense tendrils harvest matter and prey, while its Positive Energy bolt can heal a creature until it explodes.

entries.name: Elemental Energy Pod
entries: The {@creature Elemental Energy Pod|MECIounStones} stores Positive Energy in grape-like nodules. Its attacks rupture these reservoirs, spells feed new growth, and a threatened Pod can detonate every remaining nodule.

entries.name: Crystal Stone Giants
entries: {@creature Crystal Stone Giant|MECIounStones|Crystal Stone Giants} descend from conquerors transformed by Crystalle's forces and bound by Quaartzz to eternal service as wardens of the grottos.

data.name: Arackle of Siljameer Varooste
entries: The {@item Arackle of Siljameer Varooste|MECIounStones} was created before the Caur-ell wars from a dozen or more extraordinary stones fused with Crystalle's aid and bound in an Ioun-sand pendant. The working nearly killed both mages and weakened Crystalle for years.

Siljameer wore it as an oath stone and symbol of law. Moorchlyne inherited it, then died to the red dragon Verhouvenaxx. Centuries later the assassin Be-Ta'Ryu murdered his companions to possess it. It passed repeatedly between good and evil, leaving blood behind, before disappearing in the dead lands of Xuarphor. Later clues point toward Athen-Anarra.

Speak {@i Arum-Jazzalle} and roll on {@table Arackle Effect|MECIounStones}; random abilities use {@table Arackle Ability|MECIounStones}. Page 101 depicts the fused emerald-centered pendant and describes Siljameer merging a smaller violet stone into its structure while the stones sing.

data.name: Author's Afterword and Final Word

entries.name: Influences and Acknowledgements
entries: Matthew Hargenrader thanks decades of players, Jo, Gary Gygax, R. S. Barker, his sons Zachery and Alex, the contributing artists, and Tom Baxa. He traces his fascination to Jack Vance's Dying Earth stories, especially Morreion, and explains how the Manual of the Planes supplied an AD&D cosmological home for stones mined from dead stars. Two related articles appeared in Dragon Magazine #174 in October 1991. Later-edition D&D feats and abilities, the Dying Earth roleplaying game, and Jonathan Drain's Kobold Quarterly work also influenced the expanding catalog.

The long-running campaign began in 1978 but repeatedly yielded to school, work, marriage, and children. Its highest-level characters remained below the power required to confront Crystalle directly. The author closes by suggesting that the catalog may still grow through new stones and Ioun-based devices.

entries.name: Page 103: Piphany
entries: An elf crosses water-covered quicksand with a pale yellow stone while enchanted vines seize her pursuers.

entries.name: Final Word
entries: Page 104 returns the stones to their Vancian origin: on a flawlessly polished plain in the heart of a dead star, nests of black dust mark the places where Ioun Stones wait to be harvested before annihilating Nothing overtakes the seeker.
